annotation_description: Playing Undercity Sewers on turn 1 means it enters tapped, leaving no mana available this turn. With Orcish Bowmasters in hand (a flash creature that could be cast on the opponent's turn), having untapped mana on turn 1 would be valuable. Playing an untapped land like Swamp or Island would allow the option to hold up mana, and Undercity Sewers could be played on a later turn when entering tapped matters less. The surveil 1 is minor upside that doesn't justify losing tempo. With two Bowmasters in hand, having access to mana as early as possible is important.

Playing Urza's Saga on turn 1 means it only produces colorless mana this turn (Chapter I), and will advance to Chapter II next turn, then Chapter III the turn after that - meaning it will be sacrificed on turn 3. This is very early to start the Saga clock, especially when the hand has Weapons Manufacturing (1R) and Arcbound Ravager (2) that need colored mana. Playing Island first would allow casting Aether Spellbomb on turn 2 (with Saga on turn 2), or setting up for Pinnacle Emissary's warp cost. More importantly, playing Island turn 1 and Saga turn 2 gives the same Saga timeline but with access to blue mana earlier. However, with Claws of Gix also castable this turn, the Saga's construct tokens will be slightly bigger with more artifacts in play. The sequencing is debatable but Island first is generally better to preserve flexibility and have colored mana available sooner.

Gem3F Stoic skipped their land drop on turn 2 with three lands in hand. They have Undercity Sewers as their only land and need to develop mana to cast Orcish Bowmasters (1B) or Fatal Push (B). Playing a land here is free and essential for casting spells on curve. Missing a land drop when you have lands in hand is almost never correct.

Player declined to play a land on turn 2, missing a land drop with 3 lands in hand. This is particularly important because they have Orcish Bowmasters (costing {1}{B}) they want to flash in, and playing a second land now ensures they have the mana available. Playing Swamp specifically would give them access to {U}{B} to cast Orcish Bowmasters at instant speed on the opponent's turn. Missing this land drop delays their development by a full turn.

Casting Fatal Push on Arcbound Ravager when the opponent can sacrifice artifacts to it in response, growing it and potentially moving counters via Modular. The opponent has Claws of Gix and Aether Spellbomb as sacrifice fodder, and Ravager itself can sacrifice artifacts to grow. When Fatal Push resolves, the opponent can sacrifice Ravager to itself (putting counters on another artifact creature) or sacrifice other artifacts to grow Ravager above the mana value 2 threshold (though Fatal Push checks mana value, not power). However, Ravager's mana value is always 2, so Fatal Push will destroy it regardless. The real concern is that the opponent can sacrifice Ravager to its own ability in response, moving its +1/+1 counters via Modular to another artifact creature. With Claws of Gix and Aether Spellbomb on board, one of those could receive the counters. That said, killing Ravager before it accumulates more counters is still reasonable - it's a must-answer threat in Affinity. The opponent will likely just sacrifice it in response and put the counter(s) on Aether Spellbomb (not a creature) or have no valid artifact creature target. Actually, Claws of Gix and Aether Spellbomb are not artifact creatures, so Modular counters would have nowhere to go unless they have another artifact creature. So this is actually a clean kill with no Modular target available. This seems like a perfectly reasonable play.

Playing Flooded Strand over Swamp or Island is debatable. With Orcish Bowmasters in hand (costing {1}{B}), the player needs black mana. Undercity Sewers already produces B, so any land works for casting Bowmasters next turn. However, playing Flooded Strand now means it enters untapped and can be cracked later. The key consideration is that cracking Flooded Strand triggers Wan Shi Tong's 'opponent searches library' ability if the opponent has one, but more importantly, it enables Revolt for Fatal Push. Against Urza's Saga which will create a construct token (potentially large), having Revolt-enabled Fatal Push to kill creatures with MV 4 or less is valuable. Playing Flooded Strand is actually reasonable for this reason - it provides a free Revolt trigger whenever needed. However, playing a basic Swamp would give immediate access to {B}{B} (with Undercity Sewers) allowing double-spelling Bowmasters + Fatal Push on the same turn if needed, without paying 1 life. The Flooded Strand play is defensible but the life point cost and the fact that a basic land would provide the same mana flexibility makes this slightly questionable.

message: Select a Plains or Island card
annotation_description: Fetched Watery Grave (costing 2 life) when a basic Island would have been sufficient. With Island and Swamp both in hand for future land drops, the dual land's flexibility wasn't needed — basic Island + Undercity Sewers already provides 1B for Orcish Bowmasters this turn, and playing Swamp next turn covers all color needs.

Orcish Bowmasters has flash and should generally be held to cast on the opponent's turn, where it can potentially trigger off extra card draws and keeps mana open for Fatal Push. Additionally, the player should play a land before casting spells to maximize available mana and preserve information.

chosen_display: Urza's Saga — {2}, {T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct artifa... [Activate]
annotation_description: Urza's Saga is about to trigger its Chapter III ability, which will search their library for a 0 or 1 cost artifact. Before that search resolves, they could have bounced the Orcish Bowmasters with Aether Spellbomb (paying {U} from the Island) to remove the opponent's key threat. The reasoning about Bowmasters triggering on draw is correct for the draw mode, but they overlooked the bounce mode which costs {U} and doesn't trigger Bowmasters at all. Bouncing Bowmasters would also remove the Orc Army token's power boost and reset the amass count.

Fetching Undercity Sewers means it enters tapped, so the player loses access to that mana this turn. The player already has Undercity Sewers and Watery Grave on the battlefield providing UB. With Wan Shi Tong in hand (which costs XUU) and Orcish Bowmasters (1B), getting an untapped land would be more useful. Fetching a basic Island or Watery Grave (paying 2 life) would provide an untapped land, enabling plays like casting Orcish Bowmasters this turn with mana left open, or setting up for a bigger Wan Shi Tong next turn. The surveil 1 from Undercity Sewers is minor upside that doesn't compensate for losing tempo.

Playing a second Orcish Bowmasters main phase when there's no immediate ETB trigger benefit (opponent hasn't drawn an extra card) seems like it could be better held. The ETB deals 1 damage to a target, which has some value, but Bowmasters with flash is typically better held up to punish opponent's draw triggers. Additionally, casting it before playing a land (Island or Swamp are in hand) means committing mana before seeing if a land drop changes options. However, the player only has 3 lands and wants to deploy the second Bowmasters - the ETB ping + amass does provide incremental value, and holding up mana for flash isn't as critical when the opponent is on an artifact aggro deck. With Wan Shi Tong also in hand needing UU+X, deploying Bowmasters now to pressure the board is defensible.

Casting Pinnacle Emissary for its Warp cost ({U/R}) means it will be exiled at the beginning of the next end step, giving only one turn of use. Meanwhile, the opponent has an untapped Orcish Bowmasters (1/1) that could flash-block or the opponent could have interaction. More importantly, Engineered Explosives cast for X=0 (free) or X=1 would destroy the opponent's key permanents - casting EE for 0 would destroy nothing useful, but casting it with colored mana for 2 (using Island + Mox Opal) would destroy the 2-CMC Orcish Bowmasters pair. However, EE needs to be sacrificed with {2} to activate, so it would take another turn. The Warp Emissary play is reasonable as a 3/3 body that creates tokens when artifacts are cast, but it's temporary. The bigger concern is whether Weapons Manufacturing (which is already on the battlefield providing value) or a second copy would be better, since artifacts entering would trigger both Weapons Manufacturing AND Pinnacle Emissary. Playing the Warp Emissary before combat means the opponent sees the 3/3 before blocks matter, though Haiku Truth is the active player so this is for attacking. The play is defensible but using the Warp cost means losing the creature at end of turn, and the mana could potentially be used for other plays.

chosen_display: Aether Spellbomb — {1}, Sacrifice {this}: Draw a card.; {U}, Sacrifice {this}: Return target creature to ... [Activate]
annotation_description: Bounced a tapped Orcish Bowmasters instead of the Orc Army Token. Bouncing a token permanently removes it (tokens cease to exist in hand), which would have eliminated the 2/2 body entirely. Instead, the Bowmasters returns to hand where it can be recast later for another ETB trigger (1 damage + amass Orcs 1), actually generating more value for the opponent. Alternatively, bouncing the untapped Bowmasters would have cleared a blocker for the 3/3 Pinnacle Emissary.

chosen_display: Claws of Gix — {1}, Sacrifice a permanent: You gain 1 life. [Activate]
annotation_description: Activating Claws of Gix before casting Mox Opal from hand. Casting the legendary Mox Opal first (free) would trigger Weapons Manufacturing to create another Munitions token, giving an additional 2 damage to any target when sacrificed. By spending the Island mana on Claws first, they reduce their ability to sequence optimally.

Gem3F Stoic passed on casting Wan Shi Tong with 6 mana available, likely to hold up Counterspell. However, the opponent is at 11 life with a weak board (no creatures, just artifacts), and deploying a flying vigilance threat that draws cards would apply significant pressure. Even casting for X=2 (4 mana) gives a 3/3 flyer drawing 1 card, with 2 mana still available for Fatal Push.

Wan Shi Tong has flash, so casting it during the opponent's end step would be strictly better than casting it during your own postcombat main phase. By casting it now, Gem3F Stoic taps out and can't use Counterspell to protect against whatever the opponent might play on their turn. The opponent still has untapped Claws of Gix and Weapons Manufacturing that could enable plays.
